topics.name: Model Initialization & Parameters
topics.description: Initializing chat models, standard parameters, retries and runtime-configurable models.
notes: ## 初始化聊天模型
- init_chat_model 可按 "{model_provider}:{model}" 初始化，例如 "openai:o1"；也可直接使用 ChatOpenAI 等提供商类。
- 模型名由提供商包直接传给提供商 API，新模型发布后无需等待 LangChain 更新。
```python
from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
model = init_chat_model(
"claude-sonnet-4-6",
temperature=0.7, timeout=30,
max_tokens=1000, max_retries=6,
## 常用参数
- temperature：控制输出随机性，越低越确定。
- max_tokens：限制响应的 token 总数，即控制输出长度。
- timeout：等待响应的最长秒数；max_retries 默认 6 次，使用带抖动的指数退避。
## 重试与异常
- 网络错误、429 限流、5xx 服务端错误会自动重试；401、404 等客户端错误不会。
- langchain_core.exceptions 中的标准异常带有 is_retryable 属性。
- 可重试：ModelRateLimitError、ModelAPIError、ModelConnectionError、ModelTimeoutError。
- 不可重试：ModelAuthenticationError、ModelInvalidRequestError、ModelNotFoundError、ContextOverflowError 等。
## 运行时可配置模型
- 不指定 model 时，model 与 model_provider 默认可在调用时通过 config={"configurable": {...}} 切换。

topics.name: Invoke, Stream, Batch & Runnables
topics.description: The three invocation methods of chat models and the standard Runnable interface.
notes: ## 三种调用方式
- invoke()：传入消息，等待完整响应后返回一个 AIMessage。
- stream()：返回迭代器，逐步产出 AIMessageChunk；每个 chunk 可通过求和合并为完整消息。
- batch()：并行处理多个独立请求，是客户端侧并行，不同于提供商自己的 Batch API。
```python
full = None
for chunk in model.stream("What color is the sky?"):
full = chunk if full is None else full + chunk
print(full.text)
- batch_as_completed() 在每个输入完成时就产出结果，顺序可能打乱，结果带输入索引。
- 用 config={"max_concurrency": 5} 限制 batch 的最大并行调用数。
- 在流式应用（如 LangGraph）中，即使节点里调用 invoke()，LangChain 也会自动切到内部流式模式，结果不变。
## Runnable 标准接口
- Runnable 是可被调用、批处理、流式处理、转换和组合的工作单元。
- 核心方法：invoke/ainvoke、batch/abatch、stream/astream；带 a 前缀的是异步版本。
- 默认的 batch 使用线程池并行执行 invoke()。
- 用 | 运算符组合成 RunnableSequence：上一步的输出作为下一步的输入。
- 在序列中使用 dict 字面量会得到 RunnableParallel：同一输入并发送给每个分支。
```python
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda
seq = RunnableLambda(lambda x: x + 1) | RunnableLambda(lambda x: x * 2)
seq.invoke(1)  # 4

topics.name: Message Content, Metadata & Multimodal
topics.description: Content blocks, AIMessage metadata, multimodal input and ToolMessage details.
notes: ## 消息内容 content
- content 可以是字符串、提供商原生格式的内容块列表，或 LangChain 标准内容块列表。
- content_blocks 属性把 content 惰性解析为跨提供商的标准类型化内容块，不替代 content。
- Anthropic 的 thinking 块和 OpenAI 的 reasoning 块都会被统一为 type 为 "reasoning" 的块。
- 初始化消息时传入 content_blocks 是类型安全的方式，同时仍会填充 content。
## AIMessage 属性
- 常用属性：text、content、content_blocks、tool_calls、id、usage_metadata、response_metadata。
- usage_metadata 在提供商支持时包含 input_tokens、output_tokens、total_tokens 等 token 计数。
## 多模态输入
```python
message = {"role": "user", "content": [
{"type": "text", "text": "Describe the content of this image."},
{"type": "image", "url": "https://example.com/path/to/image.jpg"},
- 图片块可用 url、base64（必须同时给出 mime_type）或提供商管理的 file_id 提供数据。
- 并非所有模型支持所有文件类型，需查看提供商文档。
## ToolMessage
- tool_call_id 必须与 AIMessage 中对应工具调用的 id 一致。
- artifact 保存不会发给模型、但程序可以访问的附加数据（如文档 id、页码）。
## 序列化
- dumpd / load 可序列化并恢复消息；load() 会实例化 Python 对象，绝不要对不可信数据调用。

topics.name: Tool Calling, Structured Output & Model Features
topics.description: Tool calling basics, structured output, reasoning, model profiles, rate limiting and caching.
notes: ## 工具调用（Tool calling）
- bind_tools 把工具绑定到模型；模型在 AIMessage 的 tool_calls 中返回执行请求。
- 单独使用模型（不用 agent）时，需要自己执行工具并把 ToolMessage 回传给模型；agent 会自动处理这个循环。
- tool_choice="any" 强制使用任意一个工具；传入工具名则强制使用指定工具。
- 部分提供商（如 OpenAI、Anthropic）支持 parallel_tool_calls=False 关闭并行工具调用。
## 结构化输出
- model.with_structured_output(Schema) 让模型按 Pydantic、TypedDict 或 JSON Schema 返回。
- include_raw=True 时返回 {"raw": AIMessage, "parsed": ..., "parsing_error": ...}，可从 raw 读取 token 统计。
- method 可选 json_schema、function_calling（强制工具调用）、json_mode。
## 推理（Reasoning）
- 若模型支持，可从 content_blocks 中筛选 type == "reasoning" 的块读取推理过程。
- 部分模型支持 reasoning_effort（如 low、high），具体级别因模型而异。
## 模型画像与限流
- model.profile（需要 langchain>=1.1，beta 功能）以字典形式暴露能力，如 max_input_tokens、image_inputs、tool_calling。
- 画像可用于：按上下文窗口触发摘要、推断结构化输出策略、按模态和输入上限限制输入。
- rate_limiter 参数（如 InMemoryRateLimiter）控制请求频率，只限制请求数量，不限制请求大小。
```python
InMemoryRateLimiter(requests_per_second=0.1, check_every_n_seconds=0.1, max_bucket_size=10)
## 提示缓存
- 提供商缓存可隐式或显式启用，通常需超过最小输入 token 阈值；缓存使用情况体现在 usage metadata 中。

questions.title: In LangChain's standard chat model parameters, what does `max_tokens` do?

options.text: Sets the maximum number of tokens in the prompt you send
Sets the context window size of the model
Limits the total number of tokens in the response, which controls how long the output can be
Limits how many requests can be sent per minute

questions.explanation: max_tokens caps the length of the generated response. The context window is a property of the model, and request frequency is handled by rate limiting.

questions.title: Which string passes both the provider and the model to `init_chat_model` in a single argument?
questions.explanation: The documented format is '{model_provider}:{model}', for example 'openai:gpt-5.5'. The other separators are not recognized by init_chat_model.

questions.title: Which failures does a LangChain chat model retry automatically by default (up to 6 times with exponential backoff)?
questions.explanation: Network errors, rate limits (429) and server errors (5xx) are retried. Client errors such as 401 and 404 are not, because retrying cannot fix a bad key or a wrong resource.

questions.title: Fill in the blank to raise the number of retry attempts above the default of 6.
questions.codeSnippet:
from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model

model = init_chat_model(
    "google_genai:gemini-3.6-flash",
    ______=10,
    timeout=120,
)
questions.explanation: max_retries (default 6) controls how many times a failed request is resent, and timeout is in seconds. The other names are not standard chat model parameters.

questions.title: What does this code do?
questions.codeSnippet:
from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model

configurable_model = init_chat_model(temperature=0)

configurable_model.invoke(
    "what's your name",
    config={"configurable": {"model": "gpt-5-nano"}},
)

options.text: It raises an error because init_chat_model always requires a model name
It ignores the config and uses a default OpenAI model
It creates an agent that picks tools at runtime
No model is fixed at creation, so model and model_provider are configurable by default; this call runs gpt-5-nano chosen through config

questions.explanation: When no model value is given, 'model' and 'model_provider' become configurable at runtime. The config passed to invoke selects the model for that call.

questions.title: Which of these LangChain model exceptions are retryable (is_retryable is true)?
questions.explanation: Rate limit, timeout and connection errors are transient and retryable. ContextOverflowError (input exceeds the model's context limit) and ModelAuthenticationError are not, because resending the same request fails again.

questions.title: What does calling `model.stream(...)` on a chat model return?

options.text: A single AIMessage after generation finishes
A list of all response strings
A coroutine that must be awaited
An iterator that yields AIMessageChunk objects as the output is generated

questions.explanation: stream() yields AIMessageChunk objects, each holding a portion of the output. invoke() is the method that returns one complete AIMessage.

questions.title: What does each `print(full.text)` call show?
questions.codeSnippet:
full = None
for chunk in model.stream("What color is the sky?"):
    full = chunk if full is None else full + chunk
    print(full.text)

options.text: Only the newest fragment of text
The final complete answer on every iteration
The text accumulated so far, growing each iteration (e.g. "The", "The sky", "The sky is")
A list of all AIMessageChunk objects received so far

questions.explanation: Chunks are designed to be summed into a full message, so full holds everything received so far. Printing chunk.text instead would show only the latest fragment.

questions.title: Fill in the blank to limit `batch()` to at most 5 parallel calls.
questions.explanation: max_concurrency is a RunnableConfig key that caps parallel calls in batch() and batch_as_completed(). The other keys are not part of RunnableConfig.

questions.title: Which are key methods of the standard Runnable interface?
questions.explanation: Runnables expose invoke/ainvoke, batch/abatch and stream/astream, where the 'a' prefix marks the async version. execute() and run_all() are not part of the interface.

questions.title: What does this code print?
questions.codeSnippet:
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda

sequence = RunnableLambda(lambda x: x + 1) | RunnableLambda(lambda x: x * 2)
print(sequence.batch([1, 2, 3]))
questions.explanation: The | operator builds a RunnableSequence: each input is incremented first, then doubled, so 1 becomes (1+1)*2 = 4. [3, 5, 7] would result from doubling first.

questions.title: What does this code print?

options.text: It raises an error because a dict is not a Runnable

questions.explanation: A dict literal inside a sequence becomes a RunnableParallel that gives the same input (1+1 = 2) to every branch. The result is a dict keyed by branch name, not a list.

questions.title: How does a chat model's `batch()` method relate to provider batch APIs such as OpenAI's or Anthropic's?

options.text: It submits a job to the provider's asynchronous Batch API and returns later
It concatenates all inputs into one prompt
It parallelizes the model calls client-side and is distinct from provider batch APIs
It runs the inputs strictly one after another

questions.explanation: The docs describe batch() as client-side parallelization of model calls, explicitly distinct from provider batch APIs. It does not merge prompts or run sequentially.

questions.title: A chat model is called with `invoke()` inside a LangGraph node while the overall application is being streamed. What does LangChain do?

options.text: It raises an error because invoke() cannot be used while streaming
It automatically switches to an internal streaming mode and fires on_llm_new_token callbacks, while invoke() still returns the same result
It returns an iterator of AIMessageChunk objects instead of an AIMessage
It drops token events and only emits the final state

questions.explanation: LangChain auto-enables streaming when it detects the application is being streamed, so token events reach LangGraph's stream() and astream_events(). The calling code still receives the same invoke() result.

questions.title: Which AIMessage attribute holds token counts such as input_tokens and output_tokens?
questions.explanation: usage_metadata contains token counts when the provider reports them. tool_calls holds tool requests and text holds the message text.

questions.title: Fill in the blank so the result is linked to the tool call with ID call_123.
questions.codeSnippet:
from langchain.messages import ToolMessage

tool_message = ToolMessage(
    content="Sunny",
    ______="call_123",
)
questions.explanation: tool_call_id is required and must match the id of the tool call in the AIMessage so the model can correlate result and request.

questions.title: Fill in the blank to send an image by URL using a standard content block.
questions.explanation: The standard image block takes a url key. image_url belongs to OpenAI's provider-native format, which nests it inside an image_url block instead.

questions.title: This base64 image block is malformed. What is missing?

options.text: A url field must also be present
A mime_type field (e.g. image/jpeg), which is required for base64 data

questions.explanation: The content block reference marks mime_type as required for base64 data, so the model knows how to decode it. A url is an alternative to base64, not an addition.

questions.title: Which ways of supplying an image does the standard image content block support?

options.text: base64 data together with a mime_type
A local filesystem path in a path field
A PIL image object in an object field

questions.explanation: The docs show image blocks created from a URL, base64 data with a MIME type, or a provider-managed file ID. Local paths and in-memory image objects are not supported block fields.

questions.title: What does this code print?
questions.codeSnippet:
from langchain.messages import AIMessage

message = AIMessage(
    content=[
        {"type": "thinking", "thinking": "...", "signature": "WaUjzkyp..."},
        {"type": "text", "text": "..."},
    ],
    response_metadata={"model_provider": "anthropic"},
)
print([b["type"] for b in message.content_blocks])
questions.explanation: content_blocks parses provider-native content into standard blocks, so Anthropic's thinking block becomes a reasoning block. The raw content attribute would still contain 'thinking'.

questions.title: What is the `artifact` field of a ToolMessage for?

options.text: It holds the raw tool output that is always sent to the model
It holds the tool_call_id used to match the tool call
It holds the name of the tool that was called
It holds extra data that is not sent to the model but can be accessed programmatically, such as a document id and page

questions.explanation: content is what the model sees, while artifact carries supplementary data for downstream use without cluttering the model's context. tool_call_id and name are separate fields.

questions.title: When a model with bound tools is used standalone (outside an agent) and returns tool calls, who executes the tools?

options.text: LangChain runs them automatically when bind_tools is called
Your code must execute the requested tools and pass the results back to the model
The model provider executes every user-defined tool server-side
Nothing needs to run; the tool calls in the response are informational only

questions.explanation: The response contains a request to run a tool. Outside an agent you execute it and return a ToolMessage; the agent loop does this for you. Only built-in provider tools run server-side.

questions.title: What does passing a `rate_limiter` (e.g. InMemoryRateLimiter) to a chat model do?

options.text: It limits how many tokens each request may contain
It retries failed requests with exponential backoff
It controls the rate at which requests are made, but does not limit request size

questions.explanation: The rate limiter only limits the number of requests per unit time, not their size. Retrying with backoff is the job of max_retries.

questions.title: Fill in the blank to collect the model's reasoning blocks.
questions.codeSnippet:
response = model.invoke("Why do parrots have colorful feathers?")
steps = [b for b in response.content_blocks if b["type"] == "______"]
questions.explanation: Standard content blocks use the type "reasoning" across providers. Provider-native names such as "thinking" are normalized by content_blocks.

questions.title: What does the `profile` attribute of a LangChain chat model expose?

options.text: A dictionary of the model's supported features and capabilities, such as max_input_tokens and tool_calling
The billing profile of your API account
The conversation history of the current session

questions.explanation: model.profile (langchain>=1.1) lists capabilities such as max_input_tokens, image_inputs and tool_calling. It contains no account, history or latency data.

questions.title: If the model decides to call the tool, what does this code do?

options.text: Prints nothing, because bound tools run silently
Prints "It's sunny in Boston.", because bind_tools executes the tool
Prints each requested tool name and its arguments; get_weather itself has not been executed
Raises an error because tool_calls exists only on ToolMessage

questions.explanation: tool_calls on the AIMessage lists the model's requests (name, args, id). Nothing runs until your code invokes the tool.

questions.title: Which are documented uses of model profile data?

options.text: Summarization middleware can trigger based on the model's context window size
They automatically raise the provider's rate limits
Structured output strategies in create_agent can be inferred, e.g. by checking native structured output support
They encrypt API keys before requests are sent
Model inputs can be gated based on supported modalities and maximum input tokens

questions.explanation: Profiles let applications adapt to model capabilities, such as context size, structured output support and modalities. They have no effect on quotas or key handling.

questions.title: What does `sorted(response.keys())` print?
questions.codeSnippet:
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Movie(BaseModel):
    """A movie with details."""
    title: str
    year: int

structured = model.with_structured_output(Movie, include_raw=True)
response = structured.invoke("Provide details about the movie Inception")
print(sorted(response.keys()))
questions.explanation: With include_raw=True the result is a dict with the raw AIMessage, the parsed object and parsing_error. Without it, you would get the Movie instance directly.
